verify.note: Figure sites: original and patched draw from one state (registers, every write outside the shadow, none to the real shadow, the scratch writes = the shadow writes moved by 0x4000; H' and stack bytes proven dead). Copier entry: the commit, then the figures drawn since the last copy, modelled from their graphics and masks, against the original's shadow bytes and against the visible sprites pixel for pixel. Units: every site at four speeds, the copy as a hide; five negative controls.

status.title: Jack the Nipper
status.build: jack_the_nipper_sprites.nex: every figure (pickups and effects too) a 4-bit sprite, black lines, the body in the paper of the cell under its feet; scenery, HUD and text on the ULA
status.software: RZX replay verify of the whole recording (draws, copies, picture), units + 5 negative controls; JNext: figures show as sprites
status.next: the owner tests in JNext / on a Next; colour sheets and recolour; cheats in the .nxc

techniques.target: the game's own figure draws land in a scratch shadow at slot 1 (RES 6,H at the two returns from 0x87BB)
4-bit tile pairs keyed by graphics address + pair, never evicted within an update
every hook gives back the caller's NR 7
no frame sync: the work is the pace; hooks add 1.87 %

pacing.coverage: Simulator over the first 3,000 frames (653 updates); no JNext or hardware timing.
pacing.result: No frame sync; the hooks add 1.87 % of the time, so the game runs about 2 % slower.

dependencies.coverage: scan --writers over 30,000 frames; the verifier over the whole recording.
dependencies.result: No logic reads figure pixels; R never read; H' and the moved stack bytes dead.

feasibility.decision: Scratch-shadow redirect at slot 1 + 4-bit sprites committed at the copier's entry.
feasibility.next_experiment: JNext pace against the original (verify.update-locked-pace): within 3 %.

results.scope: 1 human recording, 108,043 frames; no hardware; JNext start only
